races.name: Al Basti Equiworld, Dubai Apprentice Handicap

runners_data.name: Rory Rocket
runners_data.note: Three wins from six starts at 6f on good ground makes this trip and surface a genuine sweet spot; hold-up style suits a race where pace builds, and Jude Fernandes has shown he can time a late challenge, but a truly modest gallop set by Calafrio is the main threat to his chance.
runners_data.comment: Rory Rocket won last time out and also scored three starts back, form that puts him top of our figures for this. Fresh from a 32-day break and with today's trip and ground already proven, the only slight query is a below-par 6th sandwiched in between.

runners_data.name: Dark Sun
runners_data.note: Consistent sort who showed a win at 5f on good ground recently and has placed four times in his last five similar-surface starts; races from off the pace and needs Calafrio to set a genuine enough tempo to reel back — headgear (p) suggests he can be on his mettle.
runners_data.comment: Dark Sun won last time out but that followed a mixed run, including consecutive fourths and a runner-up, in the five starts before it. Fresh off 28 days and with today's trip and ground proven, she rates only fifth of six here on our figures.

runners_data.name: Calafrio
runners_data.note: Sole front-runner and the key pace influence in this race; his 189-day absence is a real flag given George Baker's trainer-14 strike rate of 0/6, and though he has won over this course and distance on standard ground before, the fitness query after such a layoff could see him tied up if pressed late — but he gets a free lead.
runners_data.comment: Calafrio won three starts back and has form over today's trip and going, giving her claims among the dangers here. The concerns are two subsequent fifths and a 189-day absence since that win, leaving obvious questions over her readiness fresh into this.

runners_data.name: Lahina Bay
runners_data.note: Most likely to race prominently behind Calafrio in a natural stalking role, which is the tactically favoured position given the controlled pace; Rachel Cook and John Bridger send him here 19 days after his last run in fair order, and his five placings at 6f on similar surfaces suggest he finds one too good more often than not, but consistent.
runners_data.comment: Lahina Bay is winless in her last five starts, mixing minor-placed thirds with midfield efforts down to sixth, and sits bottom of our figures. Fresh off 19 days with today's trip and going proven, but there is little here to suggest a step forward.

runners_data.name: Be An Angel
runners_data.note: Ran into form with a recent third and showed ability on good ground earlier in career; by inclination a hold-up horse, though the field's density of closers means he is likely to end up racing closer to the pace than his natural style demands — Rod Millman's T14 of 1/20 reflects a yard not in the hottest vein, and the style compromise tempers his prospects here.
runners_data.comment: Be An Angel is yet to win in her last five starts but rates well above her official mark on our figures, second only to the selection here. The worry is a yard out of form, managing just a 5% strike this fortnight.

runners_data.name: Snooker Mccrew
runners_data.note: Returns after a 683-day absence for Max Comley, who has sent out 0/7 runners in the past fortnight — the layoff alone is a significant concern and his best form came over 7f-8f on standard, making this shorter trip on faster ground an additional question mark; a hold-up horse by nature, he is unlikely to get that position cleanly with so many rivals sharing his instinct.
runners_data.comment: Snooker McCrew won two starts back and has form over today's trip and going in his favour. The major concern is a 683-day absence from the track since, a huge fitness unknown fresh into this.

races.paceDynamic: Calafrio is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with just six runners and no genuine rival to press him, he is set to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop over Salisbury's straight six furlongs on good-to-firm ground. Lahina Bay will look to track him prominently, but the true hold-up horses — Rory Rocket and Dark Sun — are the natural closers in this field, while Be An Angel and Snooker Mccrew are also hold-up types by inclination but have been redistributed to midfield on the map because the rear is overcrowded with their profile. With Calafrio able to control tempo without being pressured, the pace is unlikely to be brutal, which marginally favours horses capable of racing off a modest gallop rather than pure sit-and-sprint closers — making the prominent-to-midfield profile the preferred tactical slot, with Lahina Bay best placed to exploit that shape and genuine hold-up horses needing the pace to lift significantly to reel Calafrio back in.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Calafrio Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Calafrio sets a measured, uncontested pace and the hold-up horses lack the room or acceleration to close on good-to-firm ground.
scenarios.body: Calafrio dictates from the front, Lahina Bay tracks in a perfect stalking position and pounces if Calafrio tires in the final furlong, with the tempo never truly hot enough to set up a late charge from further back.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Storm Home
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens sufficiently in the first half to stretch the field and create space for the genuine closers to produce a finishing burst.
scenarios.body: Rory Rocket and Dark Sun, both proven at 6f on good ground and with recent winning form, get a clear run from the rear and overhaul a tiring Calafrio; Rory Rocket in particular has won three of his last five at this trip and trip.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Types Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Calafrio's early pace is fractionally quicker than expected and the hold-up runners redistributed to midfield get a better-than-mapped position.
scenarios.body: Be An Angel or Snooker Mccrew, both natural hold-up horses racing closer to the pace than suits them, benefit from a pace collapse rather than a late sprint; their style-fit discounts make this shape marginal and reliant on the race falling unusually.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Steady Pace Suits Tracker
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop is particularly dawdling and the race turns into a sprint finish in the final two furlongs, favouring the horse with the sharpest turn of foot from a prominent position.
scenarios.body: Lahina Bay, who has placed consistently in similar conditions, benefits from a pure sprint-finish scenario; Calafrio, already in front, would need to find significant extra but has been absent 189 days which may blunt his peak effort.

watchPoints.text: Calafrio's 189-day absence is the pivotal unknown — watch whether he travels smoothly in the early furlongs or shows signs of ring-rustiness, as his ability to maintain the lead into the final furlong will determine the entire race shape.

Rory Rocket has won three of his last five at 6f on good ground and Jude Fernandes will be looking to time his challenge; watch whether Calafrio's gallop is strong enough to leave him with a genuine target to run down.

Snooker Mccrew's 683-day layoff and trainer's 0/7 recent form makes him a significant drifter risk — any market move would be meaningful given those flags, but the more likely outcome is he needs the run badly.

Lahina Bay's draw and early stride will be worth watching at the break — if he slots in directly behind Calafrio from the outset, he is in the ideal position for a race that looks set to be run at a controlled tempo.

Be An Angel and Snooker Mccrew are both natural hold-up horses who may find themselves racing closer than comfortable; watch whether they attempt to settle mid-division or get caught up in an early jostle that costs them their rhythm.

races.name: Simon & Nerys Dutfield Memorial British EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Richard 'Dick' Robathan Memorial Fillies' Handicap

runners_data.name: Gloryous
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer with form figures of 2nd and 3rd in recent good-ground handicaps at this trip, handled by the reliable William Carson; needs a strong pace to peel wide and close, which the expected steady tempo may not generate.
runners_data.comment: Gloryous tops our figures here. A third four starts back is the anchor of her form, backed by a runner-up run three starts back. She has since dipped to sixth and eighth in her last two, so the query is whether that shape returns fresh after 12 days.

runners_data.name: Pomme Pomme
runners_data.note: 86 days off the track is the key concern here — Rose Dawes claims 5lb which helps the burden, but the market will tell whether Jack Channon has her ready; when fresh in good ground she ran well, and she's a closer who needs things to stack up pace-wise.
runners_data.comment: Pomme Pomme won five starts back. She was runner-up two starts back, form that underpins her rating of 82, with the yard among the in-form 26% this fortnight. A below-par ninth last time and 86 days off the track are the concerns fresh into this.

runners_data.name: Food For Thought
runners_data.note: Unclassified style leaves genuine tactical flexibility — Ralph Beckett's filly won over 10f on good ground last time and Hector Crouch can place her wherever the race dictates; the unknown style is either an asset or a risk depending on how the shape develops.
runners_data.comment: Food For Thought won last time out. A runner-up run three starts back adds substance, and she carries an official rating of 82. Fresh from a 16-day gap with today's trip and ground proven, our figures still rate her only fifth of six here.

runners_data.name: Mayaada
runners_data.note: Ollie Sangster's filly has winning form at this trip on good ground and a solid strike-rate in similar conditions, but she is a natural hold-up type and with several rivals seeking the same rear position she is unlikely to get the unobstructed late run her style demands — discount accordingly.
runners_data.comment: Mayaada was runner-up last time out and has been placed in three of her last six starts, including a win four starts back, and is fresh into this after just 14 days. Proven over today's trip and ground, the only blot is one unplaced effort three starts back.

runners_data.name: Oh Yes You Do
runners_data.note: The race's sole front-runner and David Menuisier's charge has won twice at trips around this distance, but her style-fit flag acknowledges she is stepping into a more demanding race; unchallenged, she sets her own fractions, but she needs to conserve enough to hold on in the straight.
runners_data.comment: Oh Yes You Do won last time out and has landed two of her last five starts, with a placed effort three starts back and both trip and ground proven. The blot is a tendency to alternate, finishing fourth twice among those starts, fresh off a 23-day gap.

runners_data.name: Silver Lake
runners_data.note: William Haggas's filly has limited exposed form — just three runs, one at this trip in standard conditions — and as a genuine hold-up type pushed into a midfield slot by the congestion of closers, her chance is compressed by the race shape; headgear is noted (t) and the 64-day break adds uncertainty.
runners_data.comment: Silver Lake is winless in her last three starts, following 7th and 6th with only a modest third last time out, and is fresh off a 64-day break. The trainer's strong recent form (29% this fortnight) is the shred of encouragement in an otherwise thin profile.

races.paceDynamic: Oh Yes You Do is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no rival likely to seriously contest the early lead, she will dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop over this 1m2f on good-to-firm ground at Salisbury. The pace she sets is unlikely to be searching — a single, unchallenged leader rarely stretches a field wide enough to string rivals out, meaning the tempo will be honest but not punishing. Behind her, Gloryous, Pomme Pomme, Mayaada and Silver Lake are all natural hold-up types, while Food For Thought's style is unclassified, creating a congested rear group that will be racing for a single sustained run in the straight. This shape — a lone leader, modest gallop, compressed chasing pack — strongly favours a prominent racer who can travel just behind Oh Yes You Do and pounce entering the home straight, rather than a pure closer who needs a strong pace to pick off tired rivals; note that Mayaada and Silver Lake are genuine hold-up horses pushed into a midfield mapping because the field contains more rear-end types than the race shape can accommodate, and neither is likely to secure the wide-open track position a true hold-up move requires.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lone Leader Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Oh Yes You Do bowls along uncontested and sets a steady, metronomic gallop that keeps the hold-up pack bottled behind her.
scenarios.body: She dictates every fraction, the pace never becomes hot enough to play into closers' hands, and a horse with the tactical speed to track her or make a quick move two furlongs out wins comfortably.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Closes
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is strong enough or the home straight long enough for a sustained late run to get from the rear.
scenarios.body: A genuine closer gets a clean passage on the outside late and mows down a tired Oh Yes You Do, but the modest expected tempo makes this harder to execute than it appears.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Contested Early, Quickening Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Food For Thought or another runner pushes up to challenge Oh Yes You Do for the lead in the first half-mile, lifting the tempo.
scenarios.body: A fractionally stronger gallop rewards horses with a good turn of foot at the two-furlong marker rather than pure stamina, and a horse who can quicken off a stronger pace benefits.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaotic Reshuffled Order
scenarios.trigger: If the congested hold-up group gets badly baulked or checks sharply rounding the bend, scrambling the normal running order.
scenarios.body: Traffic trouble in the chasing pack promotes whichever runner finds a gap earliest, and a prominent type who has stolen a march on the disrupted group collects.

watchPoints.text: Oh Yes You Do gets a completely uncontested lead and is never asked a question until the home turn — watch for Joe Leavy keeping fractions deceptively slow, making it a sprint for the hold-up horses.

Mayaada and Silver Lake both want a hold-up position in a field where several rivals share that intent — monitor the early stages for congestion and checking behind the leader that could cost either horse several lengths.

Pomme Pomme returns after 86 days off; watch the market move in the final hour — if Rose Dawes is bullish early she may be trained to a peak, but a drifting price from a big yard would confirm the layoff is a genuine concern.

Food For Thought's unclassified style means Hector Crouch has a free choice of where to slot — if he pushes forward to sit second, Scenario C becomes meaningfully more likely and the pace dynamic shifts.

races.name: Redbrook Clinic Handicap

runners_data.name: Zipwire
runners_data.note: Progressive 3yo hold-up filly whose form string shows a consistent climb through the handicap ranks with back-to-back wins at 10f on Standard, though today's Good to Firm ground is untested ground for her; Millie Wonnacott's 5lb claim is useful and she arrives 26 days fresh, but she will need the pace to genuinely collapse in the final furlong to get involved from her habitual rear position.
runners_data.comment: Zipwire won five starts back and has proven form over today's trip, form that keeps him top of our figures in this field. The worry is a recent slide, finishing 5th and 6th in his last two starts, fresh off a 26-day break.

runners_data.name: Spirit Of Athene
runners_data.note: The sole front-runner in the race and therefore holds a near-unassailable tactical advantage in dictating terms, but a 206-day absence for the Ed Walker yard is a significant fitness flag and her three runs at 8f on Standard do not prove she truly stays 1m2f on quick ground; if she gets to the front uncontested she sets her own fractions, which is the single biggest factor in this race.
runners_data.comment: Spirit Of Athene won last time out. A third two starts back fills out useful recent form that puts her among the dangers here. The obvious concern is a 206-day absence since that win, a stiff test fresh off such a layoff.

runners_data.name: Three Socks On
runners_data.note: In solid form with two recent wins including a 10f success at Sandown, and the prominent style means Owen Lewis can slot in just off Spirit Of Athene and be on the wheel throughout; the 5lb claim helps offset a modest OR of 64, and this trip on Good to Firm looks perfectly within range for a horse who handles quick ground.
runners_data.comment: Three Socks On has been on an upward curve, following an eighth with back-to-back wins and a solid third last time out, arriving fresh off 29 days with today's trip already proven. The blip was a below-par fourth two starts back, but the shape overall reads progressive.

runners_data.name: Evening Fades
runners_data.note: Quietly held hold-up filly from the William Haggas yard whose form figures of 4-6-4 suggest consistency without a win at this level yet; the trip and going appear acceptable, but with two other closers in this small field she may find herself boxed in behind a slow-run race with nowhere to go until the straight, and Darragh Keenan will need to be sharp to find daylight.
runners_data.comment: Evening Fades is winless in her last three starts, sandwiching a below-par sixth between two similar fourths, and sits bottom of our figures for this. She does arrive fresh off 24 days with today's trip already proven, but there is little here to inspire confidence.

runners_data.name: Shirakawa
runners_data.note: Returned to form with a recent 10f win on Good at this course, which is the most relevant piece of evidence in the field; naturally a hold-up type whose true style has been compressed toward midfield on the map given the congested rear, but Eve Johnson Houghton's runner should be trusted to travel well within herself and produce a genuine late effort — the STYLE_FIT flag is context rather than condemnation, and the course form is the key angle.
runners_data.comment: Shirakawa won last time out having managed only a fourth and two sevenths in the three starts before that, so the form is patchy despite that recent success. Fresh off 36 days with today's trip already proven, the query is whether last time's improvement can be repeated.

races.paceDynamic: Spirit Of Athene is the only confirmed front-runner in this five-runner field and, with no rival likely to seriously contest the lead, she is set to dictate from the front at a sustainable, unforced gallop over Salisbury's 1m2f. Three Socks On has prominent tendencies and may track Spirit Of Athene into second position, while the hold-up trio of Zipwire, Evening Fades, and Shirakawa will be committed to rearward roles, chasing down a pace that may never become truly testing. On Good to Firm ground (the going report for the 6:40 1m2f confirms Good to Firm conditions despite the official Good declaration), a controlled lead with a steady-to-moderate tempo is the most probable race shape, and that profile historically rewards horses who can travel close to the pace rather than those needing a strong gallop to close into. The tactical verdict is clear: prominent-to-tracking types who can exploit the modest pace and produce their finishing effort from a live position are favoured, with deep closers at a significant disadvantage if Spirit Of Athene is never truly pressured. Note that Shirakawa is a genuine hold-up type redistributed to a midfield position on the map because the rear of this small field is already crowded with closers; in reality Spirit Of Athene and Three Socks On are best placed to secure the forward positions that will matter most.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Lead Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Spirit Of Athene bowls along in front without challenge and the pace is never truly set alight, the race is run to her rhythm.
scenarios.body: Spirit Of Athene controls the tempo from the outset, and with no horse willing or able to pressure her, she reaches the straight with a healthy lead and enough reserves to repel closing efforts on quick ground. Three Socks On, tracking closely in second, is best placed of the chasers to benefit if the winner weakens slightly, while deep closers are left with too much ground to make up.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Closer Gets Through
scenarios.trigger: If Spirit Of Athene's long absence (206 days) leaves her short of peak fitness and she fades inside the final furlong, inviting a late run.
scenarios.body: A modest overall tempo means the race may not truly test the leader until the final two furlongs, but a fitness deficit after six months off could see Spirit Of Athene tighten up late, creating just enough of a gap for Zipwire — the most progressive hold-up type in the field — to thread through. Zipwire's recent form shows strong improvement and the step up to this trip suits.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Battle Home
scenarios.trigger: If Three Socks On is ridden more aggressively and pressures Spirit Of Athene from the outset, turning the race into a two-horse duel.
scenarios.body: Three Socks On's recent wins at 8f and 10f suggest he is in form, and if Owen Lewis elects to sit upsides rather than track, the race becomes a genuine duel from halfway with both horses potentially flattening out in the closing stages. This suits any horse with hidden stamina who can sustain an honest gallop, and Evening Fades — quietly consistent at this trip — could pick up the pieces if both leaders tire.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Field Splits Wide Open
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses entirely and every runner ends up in a bunched sprint finish from the two-furlong pole.
scenarios.body: An unusually compressed finish in a field this small on quick ground could theoretically bring all five runners together, but this scenario requires multiple tactical errors and is the least likely shape given Spirit Of Athene's confirmed front-running intent. Shirakawa — a genuine hold-up type who has shown a smart turn of foot over similar trips — is best suited to a truly muddling, sprint-style finish if it somehow develops.

watchPoints.text: Spirit Of Athene's 206-day layoff is the single biggest risk in the race — if she shows any sign of blowing up in the straight after setting her own pace, the entire race shape unravels and closers will arrive late.

Three Socks On could be ridden more aggressively than expected by Owen Lewis, and if he elects to press Spirit Of Athene rather than track her, watch for an unplanned duel that inflates the pace and opens the race up for hold-up horses.

Shirakawa won over this exact course and trip on Good ground recently and should not be ignored despite the redistribution note — if any closing move is going to land, hers has the strongest course evidence behind it.

The going report confirms Good to Firm for the 6:40 1m2f slot, which is meaningfully quicker than the official Good declaration — any horse with a going concern on fast ground (particularly those with soft-ground form) should be assessed against this, not the card going.

With only five runners and a lone front-runner, early positions will be settled almost instantly — watch the first two furlongs to see whether Three Socks On commits to tracking or whether the hold-up trio all sit in a cluster, which would effectively hand Spirit Of Athene an uncontested lead and substantially increase her winning chance.

races.name: Taste The World Handicap

runners_data.name: Zen Diva
runners_data.note: Won on Good ground over 6f last time out and steps up from a minor hold at Goodwood; Ralph Beckett's filly carries a [STYLE_FIT] flag as her natural style is prominent rather than lead, but in this small field she defaults to the front by process of elimination, and her recent winning form over course-and-distance conditions is the key angle.
runners_data.comment: Zen Diva won last time out and has been consistently competitive, following a fourth with places of second and third, form that keeps her firmly among the dangers here. She is fresh off 55 days, the only slight query into this small field.

runners_data.name: The Lost Sock
runners_data.note: Roger Varian's gelding is a genuine hold-up type who needs strong fractions to land a blow, but his best form figures have come on Standard (artificial) surfaces rather than turf Good, and a modest pace in a four-runner affair is the worst-case environment for his style; the headgear (blinkers) may sharpen his early response but is unlikely to fundamentally alter his positional needs.
runners_data.comment: The Lost Sock is yet to score in his last six starts, but a second last time out fits a pattern of sporadic placed efforts, and he rates clear at the top of our figures. Quick to reappear after 9 days, he is the one to beat here.

runners_data.name: Charlie Boyo
runners_data.note: Clive Cox's gelding owns the most compelling recent form in the field — a 6f win on Good ground just seven days ago — and the tongue tie is carried forward; as a hold-up horse he faces the same moderate-pace concern as the others, but his demonstrated ability to win on identical conditions over the same trip makes him the most dangerous closer if the pace does enough.
runners_data.comment: Charlie Boyo won last time out just 7 days ago, a confident return after a mixed recent stretch, a ninth two back, but a runner-up among those earlier runs. With today's trip proven, the fast turnaround makes him the chief threat to the selection despite sitting third of three on figures.

runners_data.name: Remi Mae
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's filly is a true hold-up runner who has been mapped to midfield purely because the field contains more rear-of-the-field types than the visual space allows; her 14-day freshener is a minor positive and she showed a placed effort on Good at 6f, but the OR drop to 69 and the constrained pace scenario limit her realistic prospects, and her natural style is least suited to the expected race shape.

races.paceDynamic: Zen Diva is the lone confirmed front-runner in this four-runner field and, with no rival likely to seriously contest the early lead, she can dictate an unchallenged, controlled tempo from the gates over Salisbury's straight six furlongs on going that is riding faster than the declared Good — closer to Good to Firm based on the going reports. With Zen Diva setting a sustainable rather than pressured gallop, the race is unlikely to develop into a true end-to-end test, which compresses the advantage typically enjoyed by hold-up horses who need a strong pace to reel in. Charlie Boyo and The Lost Sock are the genuine closers in this race, but with only four runners and a modest fractions scenario, they may find themselves unable to generate the late momentum their styles demand. This race shape strongly favours horses that can race prominently and travel into the moderate pace, converting a ground-saving position into a winning burst, rather than those relying on a strong gallop to bring them into contention from the rear.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Zen Diva Dictates Freely
scenarios.trigger: If Zen Diva leads unopposed and sets a controlled, honest gallop that denies hold-up horses a true test.
scenarios.body: Zen Diva bowls along at the front without any pressure from the small field, dictating fractions and conserving energy for the closing stages; horses coming from off the pace on a moderate tempo find the gap to the leader never increases enough to be exploited.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Reel In Late
scenarios.trigger: If Zen Diva sets a slightly faster-than-expected gallop that strings out the field and leaves something for hold-up horses to aim at.
scenarios.body: A stronger early pace empties Zen Diva in the final furlong and allows the hold-up horses to pick up momentum with clear targets ahead; Charlie Boyo, with the best recent form including a 6f win on Good, is best placed among the closers to capitalise.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Remi Mae Springs Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses entirely in the final two furlongs and Remi Mae, finding more natural ground from a wider trip drop, launches a powerful late run.
scenarios.body: Remi Mae has been competitive on Good ground at 6f and, if the redistribution to midfield accidentally suits the tempo, she could emerge as a late threat; however her hold-up style is genuinely constrained in a small, slowly-run field, making this a low-probability outcome.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: The Lost Sock Improves
scenarios.trigger: If recent form is misleading and The Lost Sock rediscovers the level of his best efforts, travelling prominently enough to challenge.
scenarios.body: The Lost Sock's form string is patchy and his best efforts have come on Standard going rather than Good, making this scenario reliant on a step forward that the data does not strongly support; without a pace collapse or a tactical error from Zen Diva, he is unlikely to find the required improvement.

watchPoints.text: Zen Diva's early behaviour is critical — if she is slow from the gates or fails to assert immediately, the entire race shape collapses and hold-up horses gain a decisive advantage.

Charlie Boyo ran just seven days ago and connections are clearly happy with the quick turnaround, but any residual fatigue in the closing stages could cost him if the pace is truly modest and a sprint finish develops.

The Lost Sock has struggled on Good turf repeatedly in his recent history (10th and 7th over 5f on Good), and punters should note that the going reports suggest the surface is riding closer to Good to Firm, which may not suit his profile at all.

With only four runners, any early incident or crowding leaving the stalls on Salisbury's straight track could disproportionately disrupt the small field — watch for a clean break from Zen Diva in particular.

Remi Mae's redistribution to midfield on the pace map should not be misread as a change of style — she is a genuine hold-up horse running in a race shape that is structurally against her, and her price should reflect that tactical disadvantage.
